summary: Ground-truth-verified every wire-format surface named in docs/V1-WIRE-FORMAT-INVENTORY.md against actual code + tests. Inventory exists at docs/V1-WIRE-FORMAT-INVENTORY.md (the lens brief named it /docs/WIRE-FORMAT-INVENTORY.md — minor brief drift, the file IS there under the V1- prefix). Inventory format-version-discriminators + codepoint dispatch are LIVE + typed-reject works. BUT: 4 MAJOR findings + 5 MINOR. The dominant gap: the V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE.md §4 explicitly calls for hex-pinned canonical-bytes golden-string tests under tests/canonical_bytes_v1_*.rs for 8 named surfaces, and only ONE such test exists (DSL subgraph CID-pin). Existing 'coverage' is roundtrip + constant-value + format-version-byte-position pins — strong but NOT the hex-pinned golden-bytes the freeze contract names. Also: a real DOC↔CODE drift on AAD layout (doc claims AAD binds (chunk_index, total_chunks, plaintext_cid); code binds only (plaintext_cid, chunk_index)) — freezing the doc would commit to bytes the code doesn't produce. Also: phantom citations (4 cited test files don't exist; named coverage is in differently-named files). Disposition: FIX-NOW (per HARD RULE 12). The freeze cannot legitimately land without (a) resolving the AAD doc-vs-code drift, (b) minting the named-but-missing hex-pinned byte-pin tests OR explicitly down-scoping the §4 'shopping list' to the actually-shipped roundtrip+constant pin shape, (c) fixing phantom citations in the inventory, (d) the phantom '§6 CI gate (13)' reference in V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE.md:315.

findings.title: DOC↔CODE DRIFT — AAD layout for per-chunk AEAD: doc claims tuple of 3, code binds tuple of 2

evidence.doc_claim: docs/V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE.md:314-315: 'AAD layout binds (chunk_index: u64, total_chunks: u64, plaintext_cid: Cid)' + docs/V1-WIRE-FORMAT-INVENTORY.md:74: 'AAD binds (chunk_index: u64, total_chunks: u64, plaintext_cid: Cid)'.
evidence.code_reality: crates/benten-crypto-suite/src/aead.rs:221 — `pub fn aad_per_chunk(plaintext_cid: &[u8], chunk_index: u64) -> Vec<u8>` — only 2 components: plaintext_cid + chunk_index. NO total_chunks field. AAD body: `b'benten-aead:chunk:' || plaintext_cid || chunk_index.to_le_bytes()`. Confirmed via grep: zero occurrences of `total_chunks` in `crates/benten-crypto-suite/src/aead.rs` or `crates/benten-graph/src/aead_wrap.rs`.
evidence.phantom_citation: Both doc sources cite '§6 CI gate (13)' as authority, but V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE.md has no §6 with numbered CI gates (grep confirms zero matches for 'gate (13)' / 'gate 13' / 'Gate 13' outside the citation itself).

findings.impact: FREEZE-INTEGRITY. Locking V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE.md as-written commits the v1-beta wire format to a stronger AAD binding than the code produces. A future implementer reading the doc would believe `total_chunks` is part of the bytes and could (a) add it (breaking decode of pre-freeze ciphertext) OR (b) write a verifier that requires it (failing on real ciphertext). Either way the freeze contract becomes self-contradicting at the byte level. Cross-chunk-truncation-attack defense (which `total_chunks` would actually provide; chunk_index alone does NOT defend against truncating the trailing chunks) is the security property the doc implies but code doesn't deliver.
fix_options: Option A — doc-corrects-to-match-code: edit V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE.md:314 + V1-WIRE-FORMAT-INVENTORY.md:74 to say `AAD binds (plaintext_cid, chunk_index)` matching the code. Accept the truncation-attack residual + document it explicitly in SECURITY-POSTURE.md (Compromise # candidate). Also delete the phantom '§6 CI gate (13)' citation.

Option B — code-adds-total-chunks-to-match-doc: extend `aad_per_chunk` to `(plaintext_cid, chunk_index, total_chunks)`; every encrypted blob in existence must re-encrypt under the new AAD (P-III change). Given no users yet (per the no-users-yet rationale used at G-CORE-6b SchemaVersion bump), this is the stronger choice if the truncation-attack defense is desired.
findings.recommendation: Surface to Ben as the wire-format-byte-binding decision-point baked into G-CORE-9 freeze. The freeze cannot land with the drift unresolved — locking the doc fixates the v1-beta bytes to one thing or the other.
findings.destination_if_fixed_now: V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE.md item 15(g) + V1-WIRE-FORMAT-INVENTORY.md row 4 + crates/benten-crypto-suite/src/aead.rs:221 (if Option B) + new SECURITY-POSTURE.md Compromise entry (if Option A).

findings.title: Shopping-list of 8 named hex-pinned byte-pin tests is essentially un-built — only 1 of 8 exists

evidence.spec_claim: docs/V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE.md:359-365 explicitly names the verification mechanism: 'Byte-pin tests under tests/canonical_bytes_v1_*.rs (BUILD-AT-FREEZE-WAVE: add per-shape byte-pin where it doesn't exist — shopping-list: SnapshotBlob v2, MerkleRangeProof v2 (if shipped), per-chunk-AEAD, UCAN-Varsig v1 header, AuthorizationGrant CBOR, Drop bundle CBOR, encryption envelope per codepoint, signature envelope per codepoint). Each test loads a hex-pinned canonical bytes string + asserts encode + decode round-trip + CID stability.'
evidence.ground_truth: find . -name 'canonical_bytes_v1*' returns ONLY `crates/benten-dsl-compiler/tests/canonical_bytes_v1_scheme_pin.rs` (the DSL subgraph CID-pin from #604; uses the strongest shape — pins a literal CID string). NO other `canonical_bytes_v1_*.rs` file exists. grep for `hex_literal::hex!` or `hex!(` across all test files returns ZERO matches outside per-byte tamper tests. NO hex-pinned canonical-bytes literal test exists for: SnapshotBlob v2, per-chunk-AEAD, UCAN-Varsig v1 header, AuthorizationGrant, Drop bundle, encryption-envelope-per-codepoint, signature-envelope-per-codepoint.
evidence.what_DOES_exist: Each surface has a different KIND of pin: SnapshotBlob v2 has roundtrip+strict-version-reject (tf11_*.rs + snapshot_blob_backend.rs); per-chunk-AEAD has the IROH_BLOCK_SIZE constant pin + format-version-byte-position pin (aead.rs unit tests + tf3d_*.rs); UCAN-Varsig has byte-0/byte-1/bytes-2-3-codepoint position pins (tf3a_ucan_varsig_v1_header_carries_hybrid_signature.rs); AuthorizationGrant has binding-sig + roundtrip (tf3b_authorization_grant_*.rs — NO hex pin); Drop bundle has roundtrip + version-mismatch (tf3f_drop_bundle_offline_consume.rs — NO hex pin); swap-matrix has every-arm-roundtrip (tf4_gcore3c_full_swap_matrix_*.rs — NO hex pin). These are STRONG pins but they are NOT the hex-pinned-golden-bytes-string the §4 spec names.

findings.impact: If the freeze contract's §4 verification mechanism is read literally, the freeze CANNOT legitimately land (the doc itself says 'The wire format for any surface that does not yet have a byte-pin test cannot legitimately freeze; even an inventory entry without a fixture is just narrative' — V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE.md:352-354). If the freeze contract is read pragmatically (roundtrip + structural-position pins ARE byte-pins for purposes of detecting regressions), then the §4 'shopping list' language needs to down-scope to the shipped shape. Either way the doc + code don't agree on what was built.
fix_options: Option A — build the shopping list: dispatch a fix-pass wave authoring `crates/benten-graph/tests/canonical_bytes_v1_snapshot_blob.rs` + `crates/benten-crypto-suite/tests/canonical_bytes_v1_aead_envelope_per_codepoint.rs` + `crates/benten-crypto-suite/tests/canonical_bytes_v1_varsig_per_codepoint.rs` + `crates/benten-caps/tests/canonical_bytes_v1_authorization_grant.rs` + `crates/benten-drop/tests/canonical_bytes_v1_drop_bundle.rs` — each builds a fixture, encodes to canonical bytes, asserts the hex-encoded bytes match a checked-in golden hex string + round-trips. ~5 files × ~100 LOC = ~500 LOC. The CID-pin shape from `canonical_bytes_v1_scheme_pin.rs:137` is the model.

Option B — down-scope the §4 spec: rewrite V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE.md:352-365 to acknowledge that 'byte-pin' covers (a) hex-pinned canonical bytes (strongest), (b) BLAKE3-pin of canonical bytes (per DSL precedent), (c) structural-position byte assertion (per Varsig precedent), (d) roundtrip + format-version-strict-reject (per SnapshotBlob precedent), with a per-surface declaration in V1-WIRE-FORMAT-INVENTORY.md of WHICH shape it uses.
findings.recommendation: Option A is the higher-conviction fix (the freeze contract IS the v1-beta bytewise lock; spending ~500 LOC to make it concrete is cheap insurance). Option B is the pragmatic-but-weaker fix. Either resolves the contradiction; surfacing to Ben as the freeze-readiness decision.
findings.destination_if_fixed_now: 5 new canonical_bytes_v1_*.rs test files (Option A) OR V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE.md §4 + V1-WIRE-FORMAT-INVENTORY.md per-surface byte-pin-shape declaration (Option B).

findings.title: Crypto-suite codepoint table integer values are NOT pinned in tests (despite being inventory item #10 'COVERED')

evidence.inventory_claim: docs/V1-WIRE-FORMAT-INVENTORY.md:196-200 row 10: 'Crypto-suite codepoint table integers — byte-pin test coverage: crates/benten-crypto-suite/tests/codepoint_table_integer_values_pinned.rs (or equivalent golden-file test) — asserts every codepoint integer matches the V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE.md item 6.2 table.'
evidence.ground_truth: find returns ZERO matches for `codepoint_table_integer_values_pinned*`. grep across the entire crates/ tree for `assert.*0x0001` / `assert.*0x0002` / `assert.*0x0003` (the SigCodepoint table integers) returns ZERO matches. grep for `assert.*0x647a` / `assert.*0x6400` (cipher-suite v1-LIVE integers) also returns ZERO matches. The ONLY codepoint integer value pinned anywhere in a test-style assertion is `0x647b` (crates/benten-crypto-suite/src/swap_matrix.rs:1846 `assert_eq!(CipherSuiteCodepoint::HYBRID_MLKEM768_HQC.raw(), 0x647b);`) and `0x647c` (crates/benten-crypto-suite/tests/tf4_codepoint_0x647c_pure_pq_mlkem_only.rs:43-46).
evidence.indirect_coverage: tf3a_ucan_varsig_v1_header_carries_hybrid_signature.rs:122 asserts the codepoint bytes parsed from wire equal `SigCodepoint::HYBRID_ED25519_MLDSA65.raw()` — this catches PARSER drift but NOT a silent renumbering of the constant itself. If someone changed `pub const HYBRID_ED25519_MLDSA65: Self = Self(0x0001);` to `Self(0x0007);` the wire-test would still pass (both sides use the constant).

findings.impact: The codepoint table IS the freeze contract (per CLAUDE.md baked-in #5: the multiformats framing IS the permanent commitment). A silent integer renumbering would change the wire bytes invisibly — wire-format-incompatible peers (anyone running the old build) cannot decode the new bytes. This is exactly the regression-class the freeze contract is meant to catch.
findings.fix: Mint `crates/benten-crypto-suite/tests/canonical_bytes_v1_codepoint_table_integer_pinned.rs` asserting each named constant against its V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE.md §item-6.2 integer value: `HYBRID_ED25519_MLDSA65 == 0x0001`, `CLASSICAL_ED25519 == 0x0002`, `HYBRID_MLDSA65_SLHDSA == 0x0003`, `HYBRID_X25519_MLKEM768 == 0x647a`, `CLASSICAL_X25519 == 0x6400`, `NONE_PLAINTEXT == 0x0000`, `HYBRID_MLKEM768_HQC == 0x647b`, `PURE_PQ_MLKEM768_ONLY == 0x647c`, `HashCodepoint::BLAKE3 == 0x1e`, `SHA2_512_256 == 0x1015`, `SHA3_256 == 0x16`. ~40 LOC, mechanical. This IS the wire-format byte-pin the inventory's row #10 falsely claims is covered.

findings.title: AuthorizationGrant CBOR has no explicit format_version field (relies on #[non_exhaustive] for forward-compat)

evidence.code: crates/benten-caps/src/authorization_grant.rs:204-246 — `pub struct AuthorizationGrant { ucan, key_material, binding_sig, audience_binding, issuer_verifying_key, audience_pubkey: Option, scope: Option }` — NO `schema_version: u32` discriminator. The two Option fields are #[serde(default)]-tail-appended for back-compat.
evidence.inventory_claim: docs/V1-WIRE-FORMAT-INVENTORY.md:119: 'Format version: #[non_exhaustive] per V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE row 8.d — future additive fields land at the tail.'
evidence.asymmetry: SnapshotBlob uses `schema_version: u32` + typed-strict-reject (the MIGRATION mechanism the freeze contract names). Drop bundle uses `DropBundleVersion` enum + `UnsupportedDropVersion` typed-reject. AuthorizationGrant uses tail-append-with-#[serde(default)] — a WEAKER mechanism that fails OPEN on future-version blobs (a v2 grant with a new required field will be DECODED by a v1 reader as a missing-default rather than typed-rejected).

findings.impact: AuthorizationGrant is the load-bearing cap-binding artifact (every Drop bundle carries one; every UCAN-blobs request validates against one). A future additive field that semantically MUST be present (e.g. a v2 'rotation_witness' field) would be silently absent in v1-readers, weakening the binding guarantee. Doesn't matter for v1-beta but matters for any post-freeze additive field.
findings.named_destination: docs/future/phase-4-backlog.md — add §X 'AuthorizationGrant explicit format_version discriminator (post-v1-beta)' row. The asymmetry with SnapshotBlob / Drop bundle is INTENTIONAL at v1-beta (additive-tail discipline) but should be documented as a known posture so a future required-field doesn't surprise the freeze. (Per HARD RULE 12: this is a legitimate BELONGS-NAMED-NOW because the destination — phase-4-backlog.md — exists and the entry lands NOW.)

findings.named_destination: Couples to MAJOR-4 fix: when minting canonical_bytes_v1_codepoint_table_integer_pinned.rs, add a sibling test (or a section in the same file) asserting `0x647a` decodes/encodes ChaCha20-Poly1305-with-X25519-ML-KEM-768 specifically (a forward-canary that re-purposing the integer breaks the test).
